info.title: Lineage Model API
info.description: Machine-facing Model API for the Lineage AI model registry: publish, resolve, fetch, and manage models, versions, artifacts, lineage, and deployments. Auth is handled by infrastructure; a trusted X-Lineage-Actor header is recorded for audit.

tags.name: insights
tags.description: Composition facts submitted by producers. The registry stores and queries them; it never derives them from an artifact.

tags.name: compliance
tags.description: Risk classification under a named regulatory regime — the EU AI Act (`eu_ai_act`) and financial model-risk management (`mrm`), one row per regime per model — plus the MRM validation record. Every class, tier and validation is something a person declared; the registry never infers one, and never changes or blocks anything when one goes out of date.

tags.name: retention
tags.description: Legal hold and the retention floor (§19). Every mechanism here is a refusal or an attestation — nothing deletes.

tags.name: reviews
tags.description: The Art. 25 modification-review queue (§17). It surfaces derivations whose technical delta may have transferred provider liability, and records what a human concluded. It flags; it never decides whether a change is substantial in law, and it never blocks an action.

tags.name: change-plans
tags.description: Change control plans (§22) — the FDA PCCP shape. A plan declares, in the §11.4 verdict vocabulary, which changes are pre-authorised; conformance says whether each derivation falls inside the plan in force when it shipped. Conformance is derived on read, never stored. It reports; it never decides whether a new submission is required, and it never blocks a publish.

parameters.name: euSystemRiskClass
parameters.description: Stored column, pushed into SQL. Selects only models classified this way under the regime — never models nobody has classified.

parameters.name: classificationState
parameters.description: Computed on every read, so this is not a stored filter. `unclassified` returns models with no row for the regime; it is not a kind of `stale`.

parameters.name: mrmTier
parameters.description: Stored column, pushed into SQL. Selects only models with an `mrm` row at this tier — never models nobody has tiered.

parameters.name: mrmState
parameters.description: Computed on every read (§20.7). `untiered` returns models with no `mrm` row or an explicit `untiered`. Combined with an EU filter, returns the models that pass both.

parameters.name: regime
parameters.description: Turns on that regime's lens without filtering on it: `eu_ai_act` embeds `classification`, `mrm` embeds `mrm`.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `classification` embeds each model's EU row, `mrm` its MRM row, without filtering on either; `classification,mrm` embeds both. Omitted entirely, this endpoint runs the same query it always has — the joins and their version aggregates are not paid for unless asked for.

get.description: Returns ModelInventoryPage instead when any classification parameter or include=classification is present.

409.description: Refused. details.reason is legal_hold (with heldSince, heldBy and, when inherited, heldSubject), retention_floor (with floorDays, ageDays), or the pre-existing production-version guard. ?force=true overrides only the production-version guard — never a legal hold and never the retention floor.

patch.description: Edits descriptive metadata only — mediaType, serviceAccount, customProperties — and is allowed on a locked version too. uri, digest and sizeBytes are immutable on every version: a changed value is 409.

409.description: Refused: the version is locked (details.reason version_locked, with lockedAt). Its artifact set froze when it first entered staging; publish a new version instead.

get.summary: Broker fetch: redirect to signed URL or stream-through
List lineage edges, or traverse the graph when ?direction is set (§07.3)

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: upstream=ancestry, downstream=impact; when set, returns a LineageGraph

200.description: Flat edge list, or a LineageGraph when ?direction is set

get.summary: Get recorded composition facts for a version
get.description: Returns only what producers submitted. A version nobody has reported on is a 404, not an empty record.

patch.description: Merges per field: an absent key is left unchanged, an explicit null clears. Several independent producers report on one version, so merging is what keeps them from clobbering each other. Unknown fields are rejected rather than dropped.

put.description: Appropriate only where one producer owns every field; otherwise use PATCH.

post.description: Append-only: a re-run is a new row with its own runAt and harness version, so regressions stay visible.

put.description: In-memory size is a function of dtype, batch, sequence length, KV cache, and framework overhead, so each scenario carries the assumptions behind it. An estimated footprint requires a basis.

get.summary: Compare two versions of a model
get.description: Computed entirely over stored facts; no artifact is read. Where the required facts were never submitted the verdict is `unknown` with the missing inputs named.

get.summary: Every regime's classification for a model
get.description: Each row carries its own state, computed against its own classifiedAt.

parameters.name: regime
parameters.description: The regime being read or written. Putting it in the path is what makes the write safe: a client cannot see or touch another regime's row.

get.description: 404 when this model has never been classified under this regime — the `unclassified` state, which appears as a peer value on the model inventory query.

put.description: PUT, not PATCH: the row is replaced whole, so an old basis can never sit underneath a brand-new class. The body carries this regime's enum (euSystemRiskClass/euGpaiTier on `eu_ai_act`, mrmTier on `mrm`) plus the shared fields. Audited as `classification.set` with the regime recorded.

post.summary: Place a legal hold on a model
post.description: Refuses any subsequent DELETE of this model, and of anything its deletion would destroy. Blocks destruction only: PATCH, transitions and archival keep working (§19.3.1).

post.summary: Release a legal hold on a model
post.description: A separate, audited action. Clearing a hold is the event an auditor cares about, so it is never implicit and never a side effect of another operation.

post.summary: Place a legal hold on a version
post.description: Refuses any subsequent DELETE of this version, and of anything its deletion would destroy. Blocks destruction only: PATCH, transitions and archival keep working (§19.3.1).

post.summary: Release a legal hold on a version
post.description: A separate, audited action. Clearing a hold is the event an auditor cares about, so it is never implicit and never a side effect of another operation.

get.description: What this process is actually running under, not what a chart intended. A filing that cites a retention period cites this number. Also echoed at /healthz on the ops port; it is on /v1 so a client with only HTTP access to the registry can read it.

get.summary: Recompute every sealed epoch and check the chain
get.description: A detected break returns 200 with ok:false, not an error status: the request succeeded and the answer is bad news. A 4xx would be indistinguishable from the endpoint itself being broken.

parameters.name: fromEpoch
parameters.description: Lower bound. A bounded scan does not treat its own lower bound as a removed epoch.

get.summary: Inclusion proof for one audit event

409.description: details.reason is epoch_unsealed (with sealsAt — the epoch is still open), not_attested (the row predates attestation; permanent), or attestation_disabled

post.summary: Record a review of one derivation
post.description: Closes a queue item. The server fills verdictAtReview from §11.4 at this moment and freezes it; a client-supplied value is rejected with 400. Audited as `review.record`.

get.summary: Every review recorded against a version
get.description: Newest first, across every edge. Superseded reviews are returned too — rows are append-only, and what somebody concluded before is part of the record.

post.summary: Record a validation of a version
post.description: Appends. Audited as `validation.record`. A self-validation (validator = version author) is recorded with independenceEvidenced false, never refused.

get.summary: A version's validation history and state
get.description: Newest first; superseded validations are returned too — what was believed before is the question an examiner asks.

post.summary: Record that a conditional validation's conditions are met
post.description: Sets conditionsClearedAt, once. 409 `reason: not_conditional` on any other outcome, 409 `reason: already_cleared` on a second call. Audited as `validation.conditions_cleared`. No request body.

get.description: Derivations on models classified high-risk or GPAI whose §11.4 verdict is not `identical`. `unknown` is included deliberately: 'we cannot tell what changed' is precisely the case that wants human eyes, and excluding it would make a missing weights hash look like a clean bill of health. Omitting `status` returns open and closed items alike.

post.description: Appends. Audited as `change_plan.declare`, and `change_plan.supersede` when `supersedes` names the open plan this one replaces — that plan's effectiveTo is set to this plan's effectiveFrom in the same write. Without `supersedes`, a plan overlapping any existing window is 409 `plan_overlap`: two live plans would make conformance ambiguous.

get.description: Newest effectiveFrom first; superseded plans are returned too — which plan was in force when a version shipped is the whole question.

get.summary: A version's conformance to its change control plan
get.description: One item per `derived_from` edge on the version, judged against the plan in force at its publish time. `no_plan` when the model has none. A version with no `derived_from` edge is 409 `no_predecessor`: there is nothing to compare.

Every `derived_from` edge on a model with at least one plan, judged against the plan in force when its version was published. `status` takes one or more values, comma-separated or repeated; `outside_plan,undetermined` is what wants a human. Omitting it returns every row. `undetermined` (the verdict is `unknown`) is queued, not passed; `uncovered` (no plan in force at publish) is not a violation.

asOf.name: asOf
asOf.description: Epoch-millis instant; return only audit events with at <= asOf. The history as it stood then, stable however much is written later. 400 invalid_argument if not a positive integer.

stageChangedAt.description: When the version entered its current stage. Moved only by a stage transition (including a demotion), never by an edit — the anchor of the MRM monitoring check.

lockedAt.description: When the version first entered staging or production and its artifact set froze. Absent while unlocked; never cleared. On a locked version artifact register, upload, finalize and delete are refused with 409 failed_precondition, details.reason version_locked — publish a new version to change files.

contentUrl.description: Server-relative path (not absolute) to PUT the raw bytes to when streamThrough is set; resolve it against the Model API origin.

ociImage.description: Pullable OCI image reference when this version's MODEL artifacts share one manifest; goes straight into InferenceService storageUri.

properties.description: How the relation came about, e.g. {"method":"quantize","from_dtype":"fp16"} on a derived_from edge.
Optional detail about how the relation came about, e.g. {"method":"quantize"}.

epoch.description: The sealing window this row belongs to (§19.5). Absent means the row is not attested — written before sealing existed, or while it was disabled. Enabling attestation does not backfill.

FactSource.description: How a value was obtained. declared = asserted by the publisher (attributed, not verified); derived = computed by a producer from the model; measured = reported by a runtime or harness, valid within its stated basis.

Hashes.description: The four-level architecture fingerprint. Separating the levels makes the diff verdict a table lookup rather than a heuristic. weights is optional: a producer that only read file headers submits the first three.

FieldSource.description: Attribution for one field. Provenance is per field, not per record, because independent producers supply different facts.

LayerBlock.description: One distinct block of the architecture, collapsed over repeats: an 80-layer decoder contributes one row with repeatCount=80. paramCount and bytes are per single instance.

weightsBytes.description: Sum of tensor nbytes; differs from diskBytes under sharding, zip, or compression.

archDoc.description: Canonical normalized graph summary the hashes were computed over. The registry reads only the per-tensor digest list from it, for the partial diff.

coverage.description: Why a field was or was not supplied; distinguishes 'the format does not expose this' from 'not attempted'.

InsightWrite.description: A fact submission. Everything under `facts` is a mergeable field; the rest describes the write, and its attribution is stamped onto every field the write touched.

schemaVersion.description: The payload contract the producer built against. An unrecognised value is rejected with 400 rather than partially applied.

reporter.description: The tool writing this record, distinct from `producer` which is the library that wrote the model files.

facts.description: Mergeable fields: framework, producer, paramCountTotal, paramCountTrainable, paramCountMethod, tensorCount, dtypeDominant, quantMethod, quantScope, diskBytes, weightsBytes, hashes, archDoc, coverage. An explicit null clears a field; an absent key leaves it unchanged. `hashes` and `coverage` merge per sub-key.

layers.description: Absent leaves the breakdown alone; an explicit (even empty) array replaces the whole set.

basis.description: The assumptions behind the numbers (kv dtype, paged attention, runtime + version). Required when source is estimated.

evidenceArtifactId.description: An artifact of kind METRICS holding the verbatim report.

higherIsBetter.description: Required: the sign of a delta cannot be inferred from the metric name.

present.description: Both sides supplied this level. Distinguishes 'reported and equal' from 'never reported'.

candidates.description: When the facts narrow the answer without settling it, the surviving verdicts.

missing.description: Hash levels the verdict needed but nobody submitted.

tensors.description: Per-tensor summary from the digests in archDoc; changedPatterns collapses repeated block indices, which is what distinguishes a merged LoRA adapter from a full fine-tune.

metrics.description: Only results sharing suite, metric, split and harness version are comparable; anything else is returned with comparable=false rather than differenced.

basis.description: Which facts each side actually supplied, so a partial verdict is identifiable as partial.

ResolvedInsight.description: Compact composition block on a resolution (?include=insight), so a scheduler can pick a device class in one call.

minDeviceMemoryBytes.description: Smallest recorded scenario total; the scenario is named alongside it because a footprint without its basis is not actionable.

Regime.description: One body of rules: the EU AI Act (`eu_ai_act`) or financial model-risk management (`mrm`: SR 26-2, PRA SS1/23, OSFI E-23). Each gets its own row per model, with its own date, author, reason and review cycle, so writing one can never move another's anchor.

EUSystemRiskClass.description: The risk class of the systems this model is used in, as declared by a person. `unclassified` is a real answer meaning nobody has said yet — it is never rendered as, and never quietly becomes, `minimal`.

EUGpaiTier.description: The model itself under Art. 53/55. A general-purpose model is not 'high risk' or 'low risk' — that is a different question, answered by euSystemRiskClass.

ClassificationState.description: Computed per regime on every read, never stored. The `eu_ai_act` ladder is `unclassified`, `stale`, `current`; the `mrm` ladder is `untiered`, `unvalidated`, `stale`, `current` (MRMState). Neither regime's first rung is a kind of `stale`.

StaleReason.description: Why a classification went out of date. `production_changed_since`: what is in production changed after the classification — a version entered production (promotion or rollback), or a file was added to the production version. Metadata edits do not trip it. For `mrm` rows: `validation_expired`, `version_published_since` (a version published after the validation), `unmonitored_in_production` (in production with no evaluation run since it got there), `conditions_outstanding`.

ClassificationInput.description: A declared assessment. classifiedAt, classifiedBy and source are owned by the server; sending any of them is rejected with 400, following the API-wide rule that unknown fields are refused rather than dropped.

mrmTier.description: The `mrm` path's enum. Defaults to `untiered`. Sending an EU field on the `mrm` path, or this on the `eu_ai_act` path, is rejected with 400.

intendedPurpose.description: Required on `eu_ai_act` unless euSystemRiskClass is `unclassified` — nobody can review a class with no stated purpose. Optional on `mrm`.

basis.description: Why this class or tier: the reasoning, not the conclusion. Required for high_annex_iii and high_annex_i, and for tier_1 and out_of_scope (422, `details.field: basis`).

reviewDueAt.description: Epoch millis, must be in the future. Null means no review scheduled, which is surfaced rather than hidden.

Classification.description: A stored assessment plus the state computed from it at read time.

classifiedAt.description: Server-set. The anchor every staleness check measures against.

classifiedBy.description: Server-set from the actor header at time of write.

source.description: Always `declared`. There is no computed path for a legal class.

state.description: The row's own regime's ladder: ClassificationState on `eu_ai_act`, MRMState on `mrm`.

staleReasons.description: Every reason that fired, not the first — someone deciding whether to redo an assessment wants the whole picture.

version.description: `mrm` rows only: the version the state is about — the production version if the model has one, else its newest. Absent when the model has no versions.

latestValidation.description: `mrm` rows only: that version's latest validation, absent when it has none.

ClassificationList.description: Every regime's row for a model. Not paginated: regimes are a closed, small set.

ModelInventoryItem.description: A model list entry carrying its classification for each regime asked about. `classification` (the EU row) and `mrm` are each absent when the model has no row for that regime — absence is the `unclassified` / `untiered` state, and inventing an empty row would put an assessment in the response that nobody wrote.

mrm.description: The model's `mrm` row with its §20.7 state, when that lens was asked for. Absent means `untiered`.

Hold.description: A live legal hold. Absent means not held — there is no boolean beside the timestamp. The *reason* for the hold is on the audit event, not here: the row carries current state, the trail carries why (§19.7.1).

heldSince.description: When the hold was placed, epoch-millis. Never refreshed — re-holding a held subject is refused rather than moving this date.

heldBy.description: The actor who placed it, from the identity header.

reason.description: Why the hold is being placed or lifted, e.g. "Regulator inquiry REF-2026-118". Required in both directions: it is recorded on the audit event and is the only durable record of the matter.

RetentionConfig.description: The retention floor in force on this install (§19.4). 0 disables a floor and is a real choice, not an unset value.

minAuditAgeDays.description: Floor on audit history. Nothing in core deletes an audit event, so this is reported rather than enforced — it is the number a filing cites.

minArchivedVersionDays.description: Floor DELETE enforces, on both models and versions.

AttestationConfig.description: Merkle epoch sealing configuration (§19.4). On by default.

sealIntervalSeconds.description: Sealing period, and the bound on the unsealed window: rows in the currently-open epoch are not yet protected.

sealGraceSeconds.description: Delay past an epoch's end before sealing it, so a transaction begun inside the window commits first. Must be shorter than the interval.

VerifyBreak.description: The first disagreement found. Names what disagreed, because "the audit log is broken" is not actionable.

kind.description: root_mismatch — a row inside the epoch was edited. leaf_count_mismatch — a row was deleted (or added). prev_root_mismatch — an epoch was removed wholesale.

found.description: What a recompute over the rows present now produced.

attestationStartedAt.description: Start of the earliest window any row was covered by. Rows older than this are outside the guarantee — enabling attestation does not backfill, because a backfilled root proves nothing.

openEpochSince.description: Start of the window still accepting writes. Rows in it are NOT yet protected — there is no root to disagree with. Bounded by sealIntervalSeconds, and reported rather than glossed.

InclusionProof.description: An O(log n) inclusion path, so a third party can verify one event without reading the log.

leafHash.description: sha256(0x00 ‖ canonical(row)). Included so a verifier can confirm its own canonicalization matches the server's before trusting the path.

leafCount.description: Leaves in the epoch. With leafIndex it determines which side each sibling is on, so the path carries hashes only.

Verdict.description: The §11.4 classification of what changed across a derivation, computed from four submitted hashes. `unknown` means the hashes do not reach — it is not a verdict of 'nothing changed'.

ReviewOutcome.description: What a human concluded. `undetermined` is a real outcome — 'looked at it, needs counsel' must be distinguishable from 'nobody opened it'.

ReviewStatus.description: Whether anyone has recorded a review for this (version, edge) pair. Computed at read time; there is no stored column.

edgeId.description: The derived_from edge being reviewed. Must be an edge leaving this version.

ReviewInput.description: There is deliberately no verdictAtReview, reviewedBy or reviewedAt field. All three are server-set, and a request that supplies one is rejected with 400 — the value of the frozen verdict is that the registry witnessed it rather than accepting a claim about it.

verdictAtReview.description: The verdict as it stood when the review was recorded. Frozen: a producer submitting a weights hash afterwards cannot rewrite what a reviewer saw.

ModificationReview.description: One human's judgement on one derivation. Append-only: a re-review is a new row and nothing is ever updated or deleted.

ReviewBasis.description: Which hash levels each side actually supplied, so a partial verdict is identifiable as partial rather than read as confident.

derivedFrom.description: The other end, when the edge points at a version in this registry.

derivedFromRef.description: The external reference the edge points at instead. A fine-tune of a third-party model is the Art. 25 case, and the one where no hashes reach.

missing.description: Which hash levels the verdict needed and did not get.

hashes.description: The full hash ladder, per level, both sides. `basis` is its two-list projection; the console draws the side-by-side fingerprints from these values.

declaredMethod.description: The edge's properties.method — the modifier's stated intent, carried beside the measurement so a reviewer can notice when the two disagree.

review.description: The latest review, on a closed item. When its verdictAtReview differs from verdict above, a producer submitted a hash after the review — worth seeing, which is why both are returned.

ReviewItem.description: One derivation in the Art. 25 queue: what changed, what the modifier said they were doing, and whether anyone has looked.

MRMTier.description: Firm-assigned model-risk tier, `tier_1` highest. `untiered` is the default and is never rendered as low risk. `out_of_scope` is a declared exclusion from the firm's framework (e.g. the SR 26-2 genAI carve-out) and requires a basis.

MRMState.description: The §20.7 ladder, computed on every read for a version's latest validation. `unvalidated` covers no validation and a latest outcome of `rejected` or `undetermined`. Neither `untiered` nor `unvalidated` is a kind of `stale`.

ValidationOutcome.description: `conditional` is fit subject to `conditions`, which are then required. `undetermined` is reviewed but cannot conclude yet.

ValidationInput.description: There is deliberately no validatedBy or validatedAt field. Both are server-set — the actor header and the server clock — and a request that supplies either is rejected with 400: the value of both is that the registry witnessed them.

scope.description: What was validated, e.g. 'credit decisioning use only'.

conditions.description: Required non-empty when outcome is `conditional` (422, `details.field: conditions`).

validUntil.description: Epoch millis, must be in the future (400). Null means no expiry, which is surfaced rather than hidden.

evidenceArtifactId.description: The report itself: an artifact of kind DOC or METRICS on this version (400 otherwise).

Validation.description: One independent judgement on one version. Append-only: a re-validation is a new row, and the current answer is the latest.

conditionsClearedAt.description: Set once by :clearConditions. While a conditional validation's conditions are uncleared, the state is `stale` with `conditions_outstanding`.

independenceEvidenced.description: validatedBy is set and differs from the version's author. A flag, never a refusal: a one-person team or a shared service account trips it legitimately, and a human decides whether it is a finding.

ValidationList.description: A version's validations, newest first, with the §20.7 state of this version against the model's `mrm` row. Not paginated.

PlannableVerdict.description: A §11.4 verdict a plan may pre-authorise. `unknown` is excluded: it is the absence of a verdict, not a kind of change.

ChangePlan.description: A declared envelope of pre-authorised changes to one model. Append-only; the one later write is effectiveTo, set when superseded.

ref.description: The submission or clearance identifier, e.g. a 510(k) number.

summary.description: What the plan permits, in the operator's words.

protocolArtifactId.description: The PCCP document: a DOC artifact on one of the model's versions. No foreign key — deleting the document leaves the plan saying what it rested on.

effectiveTo.description: Absent while open. The window is [effectiveFrom, effectiveTo).

ChangePlanInput.description: effectiveTo, declaredBy and declaredAt are not accepted: supplying one is 400.

allowedMethods.description: Omit or null for unconstrained. An empty list is refused.

effectiveFrom.description: Defaults to now. A past value is legitimate.

supersedes.description: The open plan this one replaces. Its effectiveFrom must be earlier than this one's.

Conformance.description: §22.4, derived on read. `undetermined`: the verdict is `unknown`, queued not passed. `uncovered`: no plan was in force at publish, which is not a violation.

ConformanceItem.description: One derivation judged against the plan in force when its version was published.

edgeId.description: The derived_from edge judged. A version with two predecessors is two items.

derivedFrom.description: The other end, when the edge points at a version in this registry.

derivedFromRef.description: The external reference the edge points at instead; no hashes reach it, so it reads `undetermined`.

plan.description: The plan judged against. Absent for no_plan and uncovered.

reasons.description: Why an outside_plan item is outside. Both when both hold.

hashes.description: Per level, both sides: which hashes drove the verdict.

publishedAt.description: The version's createdAt — the instant the plan in force is chosen at.
